items.summary: The FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index is set to expand from 30 to 50 stocks in the first major overhaul of its benchmark in 17 years. New constituents will be selected based on full market capitalisation, with additions announced December 3 and a phased inclusion beginning later that month—20 new stocks entering at half weight on December 21 before reaching full weight in June 2027. The change aims to reduce the index's reliance on banks and utilities, which account for nearly 60% of its weight, giving investors broader representation beyond those sectors.
items.title: Malaysia Expands KLCI Index to 50 Stocks, Spotlighting Tech and Power for 2027

As of August 2025, the company employed about 12,000 staff in Singapore and about 24,000 employees across the world.
items.title: Seatrium to Lay Off 2% of Singapore Workforce in First Restructuring Since Merger

items.summary: President Trump endorsed Nvidia's Monday decision to reinstate founder Jensen Huang as the company's CEO and president, stating on Truth Social that "the United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security." The Nvidia board had cited consultations with senior U.S. government officials in reaching its conclusion that Huang's reinstatement was not a national security risk. Trump further claimed that Attorney General Todd Blanche found no evidence of unlawful conduct by Huang, an assertion the text notes is unusual because attorneys general typically conduct such investigations independently; notably, Blanche has not yet issued a formal statement on the case. Speaking to PBS over the weekend before the announcement, Trump said Huang "he's back where he should be and we see he did absolutely nothing wrong," adding when asked about reinstatement, "I hope so, I hope so." Huang had faced accusations of multiple extramarital relationships, including one with a direct Nvidia report and another unnamed employee. The relationship most concerning to national security was alleged to involve Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, which the text states purchased billions in Nvidia chips over recent years. Concerns centered on whether ties between the CEO and Ms. Huang could have compromised sensitive information or facilitated China's access to advanced U.S. AI chips subject to export restrictions. Trump had previously stated last week that he believed this relationship did not threaten national security, noting "no one had proven she's a spy," while adding "She may not be a spy" and commenting that "China plays games with us, and we play games with China." In his full Monday statement, Trump praised the Nvidia board for returning Huang to CEO, asserted the country needs Jensen's leadership for the success of both the company and American economy, repeated that the government has no reason to believe his return poses a national security risk, claimed Attorney General Blanche confirmed the U.S. Government lacks evidence of unlawful conduct by Huang, described him personally as "a Great Patriot and National Treasure," and urged NVIDIA to continue its thorough internal investigation into compliance with U.S. export controls."}{
items.title: Trump Endorses Jensen Huang's Return to Nvidia CEO Role

items.summary: Eleven days after announcing his resignation, Nvidia announced that its board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, CEO and member of the Board of Directors. The vote followed additional meetings with Huang on Sunday, and the board said it received input from senior U.S. officials — including a call-in by the Treasury Secretary and the President (attributed to Blackstone's Hagens Berman). Colette Kress remains CFO, the independent directors' investigation into the earlier firing continues, and Jensen's Senate Banking Committee hearing is still scheduled in eight days; Nvidia also formed a board committee for national security and export control. As Matt Levine noted, because both the firing and rehiring were decided without waiting for further evidence to surface, investigators may now be positioned with an outcome that appears predetermined (AINews). The New York Times reported separately that Alice Huang was in contact with China's spy agency, while unconfirmed reports claim Trump and Vance saw no national-security wrongdoing and viewed Huang as protecting open-source models. Nvidia shares rose roughly 30%, adding about $890B in market value, though claims of suspicious pre-announcement call buying are circulating without verification (AINews). Separately, OpenAI put its base-model log-perplexity history on the record: chief scientist Jakub Pachocki plotted perplexity back to GPT-3.5 (~0.99) and GPT-4 (~0.91), with a model around 0.76 (GPT-6 Astra) showing hundreds of frontier math problems falling quickly, leading him to extrapolate another capability jump near 0.68–0.70; Pachocki proposed industry-wide development limits gated on milestones such as successors to chain-of-thought monitors, and Sam Altman tied the first common limit with concrete exit criteria to the White House Accords (AINews). Microsoft's Mustafa Suleyman gave an early endorsement by cosigning and running MAI-2 Base at 0.819 on OpenAI's evaluation set; most analysts noted that a couple more top labs — notably Anthropic, which redacted pretraining metrics from its METR report — would be needed for the effort to gain momentum (AINews). The article also covered Gemini 4 Neon positioning itself between Carbon and Hydrogen with adoption signals including first-time OpenRouter spend exceeding OpenAI's since June; Z.ai released GLM-5.4, a 750B loop transformer claiming 2T–3T-class performance via running 28 layers twice; Thinking Machines shipped Inkling Mini 2 (26.4B total/3.4B active parameters) reaching 10.04x on KernelBench-Mega ahead of Grok 4.7 and GPT-6.1-Sol; OpenAI/Cisco released Shirudo, an eBPF defense runtime; DeepMind's Gemini agents found Lean-verified quantum circuits cutting estimated compute by up to 10.9x for a fusion simulation; and Anthropic claimed a Claude-assisted roughly 250K-page proof of the Riemann Hypothesis that remains debated over whether it is truly understood (AINews). A chart plotting OpenAI's base-model log-perplexity history would show GPT-3.5 at ~0.99, GPT-4 at ~0.91 and a model around 0.76 with extrapolated capability jumps near 0.68–0.70; the series is 'OpenAI Base-Model Log-Perplexity (lower = better)'. No chart was selected for inclusion in this output.
items.title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After Government-Involved Board Vote

items.summary:
South Korea is grappling with a surge in cheating allegations at its high-stakes exams, turbocharged by AI technology. The controversy centers on the suneung, the eight-hour university entrance exam that determines candidates' lifetime economic and social standing. After Yun Jeong-hu came second in the national tax accountant exam amid online claims that top scorers cheated using AI smartglasses, he posted a 22-minute video defending his methods—naming tutors, describing late-night study sessions, and solving a corporate tax question live—to counter speculation about cheating.

The pressure to succeed has led officials to take extraordinary measures. Last week, authorities sent alerts normally reserved for air raids and nuclear attacks to every phone in the country to root out candidates smuggling electronic devices into the suneung. According to the education ministry, 111 candidates were caught with electronic devices, of whom 54 were exposed by the alerts themselves.

The government's response has included significant incentives and leadership changes. President Lee Jae Myung promised a reward of at least 100m won ($74,000) for successful tipoffs about cheating. On Sunday, education minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned amid disruption caused by last-minute changes brought in to tackle AI-assisted cheating.

Experts attribute the exam obsession partly to economic insecurity following the 1997 Asian financial crisis, when sociologist Kim Dong-chun argues exams became the accepted way of allocating shrinking opportunities because no other procedure felt fair. The 2019 scandal involving then justice minister Cho Kuk—who was jailed for forging academic credentials to get his children into prestigious schools—reinforced this belief, prompting the government to require major Seoul universities to allocate at least 40% of places on entrance exam scores.

Sangchin Chun, a Sogang University sociology professor, noted that because a single test determines lifetime economic position and social recognition, there is extreme pressure to produce good results by any means. This pressure took a dark turn when one man who scored full marks in a national law school admission exam was accused of using AI; he had planned to publicly answer part of the suneung in real time but never appeared at last week's event and was later found dead in a Seoul motel, with allegations against him unestablished.

The suneung is treated as an equalizer because it is almost entirely multiple choice and machine-marked, with no essay or interview. However, reformers argue the format itself is problematic: national education commission chair Cha Jeong-in said in August that multiple choice had reached its limits and essay assessment was unavoidable, though the plan could not gain agreement and a redesign for 2028 will keep the multiple-choice format unchanged.

Sociologist Choi Hang-seop told Yonhap news agency that South Korea has become a survival-of-the-fittest society in which doing well on the suneung or state exam is seen as the only way to survive. Chun added that memorization- and problem-solving-based assessment had been overtaken by AI technology available to candidates, with cheating flourishing in the resulting gap.

The debate over responses remains focused either on stricter invigilation and punishment or modernizing through computer-based testing. Park Do-soon, who led suneung design and became its first head, told Hankook Ilbo he no longer sees reason for humans to sit an exam where AI can get the answer in one go.
items.title: AI Cheating Allegations Intensify South Korea's Exam Obsession

A cyber criminal who hacked the maker of Grand Theft Auto has been released on licence on the same day as being sentenced to seven years in prison. Multiple offender Arion Kurtaj, from Oxford and now 21 years old, was released from custody with the judge warning him: 'Don't let this happen again.'

Kurtaj hacked several companies and individuals, including GTA 6-maker Rockstar Games, whom he tried to extort after stealing clips of the unfinished game in 2022. He pleaded guilty last Monday at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar hack and a handful of others which he carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old with the hacking gang Lapsus$.

Kurtaj had originally been sentenced to an indefinite stay in a secure hospital due to the severity of his autism. In an unusual move, he was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial and released to a normal prison in January. Now, he has been sentenced and released on the same day as the judge considered his hospital stay and remand in prison long enough.

He has been given a Serious Crime Prevention Order which will last five years. It restricts his activity online including barring him from using Telegram and Discord. City of London Police said the case 'highlights the dangers that young people can end up being drawn to online.'

Kurtaj hacked Rockstar Games, Revolut and Uber while on bail and under police protection in a Travelodge in Bicester. He was there for protection from rival hackers who had threatened to attack him for his stolen stashes of Bitcoin.

With his computer confiscated, Kurtaj hacked Rockstar using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into his hotel room television along with a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse. He stole internal company data including 90 clips showing nearly 60 minutes of gameplay from the unfinished GTA 6, which had been shrouded in secrecy until its release last week.

He then broke into the company's internal Slack messaging system to declare: 'If Rockstar does not contact me on Telegram within 24 hours I will start releasing the source code.' The company refused to co-operate so he posted the clips and source code on a forum under the username TeaPotUberHacker.

Rockstar Games said it cost the firm $5m (£3.8m) to recover from the hack, plus thousands of hours of staff time. The company also said the breach revealed for the first time that one of the playable characters in the game was a woman - a secret it was guarding closely for marketing purposes.

When he was sentenced he stood and smiled. He had short hair and an unkempt beard and wore a suit and buttoned-up white shirt without a tie. The hacker blinked frequently during the hearing.

The Judge, Mr Justice Turner, told him 'you are a very talented young man,' and warned him: 'Don't let this happen again.'

Kurtaj's defence team said he found the online world a more comfortable way of interacting with other people. They noted that 'the restricted and repetitive patterns of behaviour and interests that are a core feature of ASD [autism spectrum disorder] led him to become preoccupied with the online world where he felt better able to function and exist.'

They said he was exposed to people who showed him how to cheat at games and then to 'people who were involved in hacking.' During the pandemic, he was 'very isolated' and his 'connection to Lapsus$ provided him with a sense of community and self-worth that had been absent in his life previously.'

Kurtaj and the gang's other hacks on BT/EE, Revolut and Uber used social engineering techniques - tricking people into clicking malicious links or giving up sensitive information - to gain access to internal systems. Previously, the court heard that during his hack on Uber he posted a picture of a penis as part of his attempts to force the company to pay a ransom.

His hacks on the companies are estimated to have caused around £10m of damage. Using the data stolen from the firms, he and other members of the gang targeted cryptocurrency investors. The prosecution argued that the gang stole at least $300,000 (£230,000) from individual victims.

Kurtaj also pleaded guilty to physical assaults on workers while in custody, including multiple biting incidents. In prison, he was caught with a mobile phone after sending a taunting text message to police and posting updates on Snapchat.
items.title: GTA 6 Hacker Released on Licence After Seven-Year Sentence

items.summary: The Australian Macquarie dictionary has named "pervert glasses" as both its committee-selected and people's choice word of the year for 2026. The term refers to smartglasses such as Meta's Ray-Bans, which contain built-in cameras, microphones, and AI assistants; these have been banned at some Australian swimming pools and playgrounds amid fears they could be used to film people without consent and post the footage online. A committee of word experts described "pervert glasses" as a triumph of linguistics that reflects both the rapid acceleration of AI capabilities and widespread calls to slow this development, alongside concerns about surveillance in supermarkets and growing influence from the manosphere. The honourable mentions for the committee included "PMOS," referring to polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome linked to awareness of medical misogyny; "agentic," describing artificial intelligence's ability to make independent decisions; and "Marrickville pause," a colloquial term for conversation halting among people under Sydney's flight path. The honourable people's choice mention went to "digital dementia," which refers to short-term memory loss from reliance on technology, though the committee noted it is not a real medical diagnosis while acknowledging fears about increasing dependence on digital devices such as Google Maps and iCal. Other words featured on the shortlist included "nudify," referring to AI-generated pornography, and "AI;DR," an abbreviation for "AI didn't read." The dictionary's previous word of the year was "AI slop," which it said embodied 2025's theme of reflecting a major aspect of societal change. Both winning words are drawn from new entries in the annual online update of the Macquarie dictionary, with the people's choice winner selected through public votes on its website.
items.title: Macquarie Dictionary Names 'Pervert Glasses' Word of the Year

The procurement forms part of a broader 14 GW development pipeline, according to the article.

items.summary: SJVN Limited has commenced commercial operations of 45 MW from its 50 MW Sonitpur Solar Power Project in Assam, marking another step in the company's renewable energy expansion. According to a regulatory filing submitted to the National Stock Exchange of India and BSE Limited on November 21, 2026, SJVN Green Energy Limited (SGEL), a wholly owned subsidiary of SJVN Limited, declared 45 MW of the project's total capacity commercially operational following completion of the required trial run and certification process. The Assam Power Distribution Company Limited (APDCL) issued the Trial Run Certificate through a letter dated November 21, 2026, confirming successful completion of the trial run; the operational capacity was declared commercially available on the same day. SJVN had signed a Power Purchase Agreement with APDCL on February 7, 2024, for supply of 50 MW of solar electricity from the project, and power generated is being supplied to APDCL under that agreement. With 45 MW now operational, the project has achieved 90% of its planned capacity; the remaining 5 MW remains yet to be declared commercially operational, with no specific timeline provided for commencement of operations of the balance capacity in SJVN's regulatory disclosure. The development strengthens SJVN's presence in India's renewable energy sector and solar power segment through SGEL as it expands its portfolio toward clean energy generation targets. SJVN Limited is a Navratna Central Public Sector Enterprise and joint venture between the Government of India and the Government of Himachal Pradesh, with renewable energy development forming an important part of its long-term growth strategy.
items.title: SJVN Commissions 45 MW of Its 50 MW Sonitpur Solar Project in Assam

The Federal Reserve is expected to raise interest rates on Dec. 9, before the November inflation report scheduled for 8:30 a.m. the next morning; October consumer prices rose 0.4%, above economists' 0.3% expectation, and core prices rose 0.3% for the third straight month (per BLS data cited in the article). Fed Gov. Christopher Waller said a quarter-point increase alone "would put our credibility at risk," noting inflation is now spreading from energy into shelter, food and everyday goods after October's index jumped 0.7% following September's 5.2% rise.

The selection screen prioritized balance sheets over oil exposure: companies with small interest bills relative to cash flow and profits not dependent on a single barrel price. Five stocks met the criteria, though none passed cleanly.

ExxonMobil (NYSE: XOM) reported $17.5 billion in adjusted third-quarter profit, of which refining contributed $9.05 billion — more than half amid tight fuel markets; CEO Darren Woods attributed gains to "lasting improvements" and cited $16.9 billion in structural cost savings. The company carries $22.1 billion net debt against $19.1 billion free cash flow in the quarter, plans $20 billion of buybacks for 2027 (assuming markets cooperate), but faces production declines of about 2.5% and booked $921 million of Middle East impacts excluded from adjusted earnings.

Texas Pacific Land Corporation (NYSE: TPL) earns royalties rather than drilling; its third-quarter realized value rose to $2.40 per thousand cubic feet of gas, with net income of $167.4 million against interest expense of only $981,000 and an adjusted EBITDA margin near 87%. CEO Tyler Glover described plans for Chevron's Project Kilby data-center power plant as working toward "meaningful commercial outcomes" without promising revenue.

Valero Energy Corporation (NYSE: VLO) earned $6.8 billion in the quarter, but shares fell about 4% before the Oct. 22 opening bell on a refining margin that tripled to $39.24 per barrel; COO Gary Simmons noted Asian simple refineries earn only $2 to $3 per barrel once freight is paid and guided fourth-quarter throughput below the third quarter's 3 million barrels a day, while ending September with $9.8 billion in cash against $8.6 billion in debt.

Cheniere Energy (NYSE: LNG) saw net income of $736 million for nine months versus $3.0 billion a year earlier — blamed on derivative accounting tied to long-term gas contracts, though adjusted net income rose 27% and the company lifted its 2026 EBITDA guidance to $8.75 billion–$9.25 billion; third-quarter interest expense was $285 million versus $236 million a year earlier.

Kinder Morgan (NYSE: KMI) sold $600 million of 30-year notes at 6.15% in August, reflecting its 3.5 times net debt to EBITDA leverage; third-quarter interest expense was $430 million — about a fifth of adjusted EBITDA — and free cash flow came $120 million short of the dividend.
items.title: Five Energy Stocks Positioned to Withstand a December Fed Rate Hike

items.summary:
President Donald Trump intervened to restore Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia, demonstrating how he can wield influence despite Republicans losing control of Congress. After the Nvidia board ruled out restoring Huang following revelations about his relationships with an alleged Chinese spy and other women, Trump made a forceful case for Huang's return at a Friday press conference, then dispatched administration members over the weekend to convince the board to reverse its position in an announcement shortly before Monday's market open. Trump celebrated on CNBC, calling Huang a 'national treasure' and stating there was no national security problem after research.

The stock market soared following the reversal, while some Members of Congress criticized the move. Senate Majority Leader John Thune warned that allowing China to obtain America's most advanced chips creates a significant national security vulnerability and promised strong export control measures. Former Speaker Newt Gingrich called Huang's reinstatement 'profoundly wrong' and urged Congress to investigate it as a national security issue.

Trump's intervention extended his pattern of inserting himself into major corporate decisions, including pushing deals involving Intel and US Steel. After blocking Nippon Steel's bid for US Steel in a $14.9 billion acquisition, the Japanese company agreed to give Trump unusual power over the company's future, including authority to name a board member and final say on idling plants, production cuts, and moving jobs overseas. The administration also negotiated a 10 per cent stake in Intel by converting government grants into equity, called for Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan's resignation before announcing the deal making the US government the biggest shareholder.

Trump's team additionally struck an agreement allowing Nvidia to sell its H20 chips to China in exchange for receiving 15 per cent of those sales, and reached a deal with MP Materials that would make the Pentagon the largest shareholder in the rare earth magnet producer. Democrats vowed to investigate once they take control of Congress in January, with Huang scheduled to testify at a hearing next week.
items.title: Trump Intervenes to Restore Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO Amid Lame-Duck Phase

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee meets from 2 to 4 December, with the repo rate unchanged at 5.50% after a 0.25 percentage point increase in October that shifted its stance to 'calibrated tightening.' Governor Sanjay Malhotra said rate cuts were 'off the table in the near term,' though the committee's next decision remains unknown. Retail inflation rose to 6.09% in October from 5.54% in September, per the statistics ministry's 12 November release—above RBI's 6% upper tolerance band—with food inflation at 8.94%. In its October projection, RBI forecast full-year 2026-27 inflation at 5.2%. Banks pass repo changes to floating-rate loans: SBI raised home loan rates by 0.25 percentage points from 15 October (now ranging 7.50% to 8.80%), and HDFC Bank raised lending rates by up to 0.15 percentage points, per Business Today. Worked examples assume an 8.25% home loan with 20 years remaining: a ₹30 lakh loan's EMI rises from ₹25,562 to ₹26,035 (+₹473/month), a ₹50 lakh loan from ₹42,603 to ₹43,391 (+₹788/month), and a ₹1 crore loan by ₹1,576/month (to ₹86,782). For a borrower at 8% before October, two 0.25-point rises would raise a ₹50 lakh, 20-year loan from ₹41,822 to ₹43,391 (+₹1,569/month) and a ₹1 crore loan by ₹3,138/month combined. If RBI holds the rate in December, the October hike stays in place; borrowers should check their bank's new external benchmark rate (EBLR), its effective date, and whether their loan resets immediately or on a fixed quarterly date. Banks may raise EMIs or extend tenure: for a ₹50 lakh loan rising from 8.25% to 8.50%, holding the EMI at ₹42,603 would extend remaining tenure by roughly 12 months, raising it to ₹43,391 adds about ₹1.89 lakh in total repayments versus retaining a 20-year schedule, and extending tenure costs approximately ₹5.17 lakh more than the original schedule. These figures are worked examples, not forecasts or advice.
items.title: RBI's December MPC Meeting Approaches as Repo Rate Holds at 5.50% and Inflation Rises to 6.09%

items.summary: US President Donald Trump said he convinced Nvidia's board of directors to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang, telling CNBC on Monday that he spoke directly and indirectly with them about the decision. Describing the outcome as 'very exciting news,' Trump stated plainly: 'I made the deal.' He explained his motivation by saying he feared China could otherwise approach Huang with an offer to lead Huawei or another Chinese company, given his expertise in advanced chip technology. The claims are attributed to Trump's own statements during the phone interview.
items.title: Trump Claims Credit for Jensen Huang's Return to Nvidia

items.summary: Karen K. Lewis and Edith X. Liu present a paper titled "Valuing the Cost of Incomplete Global Markets" (NBER Working Paper 36046, 2026), which argues that deviations from complete financial markets in cross-border investments generate economic welfare costs and shows how to value these costs using standard theory and data based on three main results. The authors' first result demonstrates how welfare valuations can be derived from a general wealth-to-dividend ratio. Their second result establishes how aggregate consumption and exchange rate data can be used to uncover diversifiable goods allocations across countries. Their third result shows how asset pricing data and models can be used to value deviations from complete markets. The paper outlines a range of applications that fall under this framework, including financial intermediary constraint models.
items.title: Lewis and Liu Present Framework for Valuing Costs of Incomplete Global Financial Markets

items.summary: In a survey experiment examining how information about others' retirement regret affects annuitization and savings recommendations, Abigail Hurwitz and Olivia S. Mitchell found that responses were concentrated among individuals who underestimated their survival probabilities relative to population benchmarks, consistent with a survival belief-updating mechanism. Among these underestimators, annuity regret information increased annuitization recommendations by 16.9 percentage points (approximately 38%), while savings regret information reduced recommendations to significantly increase saving by 15.4 percentage points (approximately 28%). Less regret-averse individuals reduced aggressive savings recommendations, and the positive response to annuity regret information was concentrated among more risk-averse respondents. The annuity effect was strongest among respondents with greater annuity knowledge than less knowledgeable respondents.
items.title: Regret, Survival Beliefs, and Retirement Recommendations

On Tuesday, Nov. 24, oil prices eased to hover near a three-month low amid concern over rising crude supply and potential market surplus, even as shipping risk through the Strait of Hormuz persisted. Brent crude futures fell 40 cents, or 0.45 percent, to $88.97 a barrel by 0147 GMT after posting their lowest close since Aug. 31 on Monday. US West Texas Intermediate crude slipped 23 cents, or 0.29 percent, to $79.94 a barrel after hitting its lowest level since Aug. 26 earlier in the session.

Prices drew support from shipping risk in the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said three "violating" oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines on Monday, per Iran's Press TV. Separately, the Wall Street Journal reported—citing US officials and others familiar with the matter—that the United States is investigating whether Iran was involved in cyberattacks on as many as 50 energy tankers.

Better supply has weighed on prices, though analysts said the market remained fragile. Daniel Hynes, senior commodity strategist at ANZ, told clients that despite some improvement in inventories and product availability, "the oil market remains under severe strain." He added that while prices, time spreads, refining margins, and investor positioning increasingly suggest conditions will normalize, logistics remain constrained and inventory buffers are thin—so the system appears to be moving from acute scarcity toward persistent vulnerability rather than returning to normal.

Supply is also recovering in Libya. The country's Sharara oil pipeline has reopened, and oil has begun flowing into storage tanks at the Akakus facility in Zawiya, according to the chairperson of the National Oil Corporation speaking to Reuters on Monday.

On a global scale, Deutsche Bank said observed liquids inventory rose 52 million barrels in October—implying an oversupply of 1.7 million barrels each day—and noted that evidence is accumulating that the market is rebalancing toward surplus, though setbacks could delay progress. A preliminary Reuters poll also showed US crude oil and product inventories likely rose last week.
items.title: Oil Holds Near Three-Month Low as Rising Supply Offsets Hormuz Threat

items.summary: CrowdStrike announced it will acquire Zscaler for nearly $44 billion in stock, a transaction that could become the largest-ever cybersecurity deal. The announcement aims to generate synergies between two leading cybersecurity companies amid surging demand driven by AI hacking fears. Recent outages affecting airlines, banks, and government agencies contributed to last week's removal of the White House cyber director. Experts have attributed most of these disruptions primarily to groups using artificial intelligence to exploit numerous preexisting software vulnerabilities. A former National Security Agency official described this situation as an era where compromised technology is vulnerable to exploitation, while also clearing the way for new growth in the cybersecurity sector.
items.title: CrowdStrike to Acquire Zscaler in $44 Billion Cybersecurity Deal

Retailer Next has warned that hackers gained access to data relating to the clothing and homewares company through one of its third-party technology suppliers. The retailer, which operates more than 800 stores in the UK and Ireland along with 200 overseas locations, said on Monday it had been informed that a supplier had 'experienced a cyber incident' resulting in unauthorised access to data. Next stated that it believed customers' personal data had not been compromised, describing the affected information as 'limited in nature' and unable to be used to facilitate fraud against its customers or the company itself. The retailer said the accessed data does not include contact details, addresses, passwords, or bank details that could enable fraud, though Next's own systems were not compromised while the incident was affecting the supplier's environment. Investigations into the hack are ongoing, and Next told investors it is treating the matter with 'utmost seriousness' while working closely with the supplier, law enforcement, and regulatory authorities despite what it described as the limited and benign nature of the affected data.

The incident comes amid a broader wave of cyber-attacks against high-profile retailers worldwide. Last week, a secret UK government cybersecurity operation reportedly prevented an attack on fridges and freezers in UK supermarkets, warehouses, restaurants, petrol stations, and stadiums, following millions of euros in damage caused by hackers to fridge and freezer control systems across continental Europe. Fashion retailers including TFG London (owner of Hobbs and Whistles) and Asos have also faced cyber-attacks involving customer data access, while British retailers Marks & Spencer, the Co-op, and Harrods suffered damaging incidents last year that disrupted operations for months.

Alan Simpson of technology security firm Rapid7 expressed concern that a major retailer was hit through a supplier rather than directly. He noted that 'every online platform, delivery partner and service provider is a potential way in,' with attackers targeting the weakest link because suppliers often have more access than needed for longer than necessary without close oversight. Simpson added that while it is reassuring Next found no evidence customer data was taken, customers should be wary of unexpected emails, texts, or calls claiming to be from Next and instead visit the website or app directly rather than clicking links sent to them. He cautioned that companies sometimes say their data is safe only for the situation to change weeks later.
items.title: Next Warns of Cyber-Attack After Supplier Data Accessed

items.summary: The reinstatement of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as the company's president and chief executive has intensified congressional oversight plans and sharpened bipartisan focus on how the Trump administration concluded that his return posed no national security risk. The move, which involved direct involvement from President Donald Trump who dialed into a board meeting to push for Huang's return per Semafor's first reporting, is inflaming tensions between the president and Republicans who had joined Democrats in planning to scrutinize Huang and chip export controls on China following the scandal. After being ousted as CEO earlier this month, Huang agreed to testify privately before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, House Intelligence Committee, and House China Select Committee next month, plus publicly before the Senate Banking Committee. Trump stated that Attorney General Todd Blanche affirmed no national security risk from Huang's rehiring, though the Justice Department is conducting ongoing investigations that could affect this determination. Sen. Tim Scott (R-S.C.), who leads the Senate Banking Committee, announced Monday that Huang would appear at a public hearing on Dec. 3. Nvidia's board cited input from senior U.S. government levels in its statement expressing confidence about no national security risk. Congressional Republicans have adopted a more hawkish approach to chip export restrictions to China over the past month, with leadership in both parties leaning toward using upcoming defense legislation to address gaps at the center of the Nvidia fallout. Sen. Pete Ricketts (R-Neb.) stated Huang's behavior does not support reinstatement and that the company must answer for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips, while Sen. John Cornyn (R-Texas) questioned on X what basis supports the claim of no national security risk. Democrats anticipate continued scrutiny when they regain congressional control next year; Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Calif.), top Democrat on the House China Select Committee, noted that unknown information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from Huang remains unresolved and neither the government nor Nvidia's board has completed its investigation, calling for a full public hearing with all committee members permitted to question him. Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), poised to chair the Senate Banking Committee next Congress, said the move increases urgency of passing more stringent chip export restrictions and demanded clarification on what input was given by which senior officials. Trump's direct involvement has further fueled Democratic outrage, including from Sen. Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.).
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Reinstatement Sparks Bipartisan National Security Concerns

items.summary: The disability minister, Sir Stephen Timms, has announced plans to overhaul the assessment process for Personal Independence Payments (Pip) in order to better recognise claimants' varying costs and needs. He described the current system as 'not fit for purpose.' The review was commissioned by the government last year after it had been forced to water down planned benefit cuts following fierce opposition from more than 120 backbench Labour MPs, who threatened to vote against the legislation.
items.title: Disability minister launches review of Personal Independence Payments amid welfare reform

items.summary: Hundreds of flights were cancelled and public transport was severely disrupted across Belgium as a result of a strike against planned austerity measures. All air traffic was halted at Brussels Airport in Zaventem, home to Ryanair's low-cost operations, and at Charleroi airport. Underground services were also suspended in the capital, where large numbers of people joined a protest march.
items.title: Belgium Halts Air Traffic and Public Transport Over Cost-of-Living Strike

items.summary: Shares in Nvidia jumped 30% on Monday after the reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang, who had resigned less than two weeks earlier over an alleged Chinese spy scandal and an affair with an employee. The news helped spark a recovery across markets following a technology-led rout last week during which major indices fell between seven and 10%. Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, described Huang as the 'AI comeback kid' but cautioned that volatility was not over because Nvidia remained under scrutiny from investigators including the FBI and Capitol Hill. Kathleen Brooks of XTB noted that Nvidia's directors could see no future for the company without him. US President Donald Trump, who pressed for Huang's reinstatement, said on social media that the government had 'no reason to believe that Jensen's return to Nvidia poses any risk to National Security' and praised the board's decision.
items.title: Nvidia Shares Surge After Jensen Huang's Reinstatement Lifts Markets

items.summary: The China Manned Space Agency announced Tuesday that Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi will fly on the crewed Shenzhou-24 mission alongside Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, with Tang serving as commander. The three are a spacecraft pilot, flight engineer, and payload specialist respectively; Tang has flown in both Shenzhou-12 and Shenzhou-17 missions and is set to become the first astronaut to visit China's space station three times, while Wu embarks on his first mission from the country's third batch of astronauts. Ali will be the first foreign astronaut to reach the China Space Station. Agency spokesperson Zhang Jingbo said at the press conference that Shenzhou-24 is scheduled to launch at 8:18 a.m. Beijing Time Wednesday from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China.
items.title: China Names Shenzhou-24 Crew Including First Foreign Astronaut

items.summary:
Residents of the remote South Korean island of Ulleungdo were ordered to take shelter on Tuesday morning after several Russian military aircraft came close to entering its airspace, prompting a pre-emptive alert from the military that anticipated a violation. The defence ministry said it would summon Russia's defence attaché later in the day to lodge a strong protest.

The joint chiefs of staff (JCS) said the aircraft had entered South Korea's air defence identification zone over the Sea of Japan — known as the East Sea — and approached Ulleungdo, though they did not specify how many Russian aircraft were involved. JCS spokesperson Jang Do-young said the aircraft had approached "to the point just before violating Ulleungdo's airspace" and that a violation was anticipated because military aircraft move very fast; South Korean air force jets were scrambled before the aircraft left.

The interior ministry issued the emergency alert at 7.52am to residents of Ulleungdo, a volcanic island of about 8,700 people located roughly 120km off the east coast, telling them to take shelter. The English portion of the message read: "EVACUATION, AIR RAID." Television broadcasts were interrupted by on-screen warnings instructing residents to prepare to evacuate to nearby underground shelters and listen to broadcasting, and the alert was lifted at 7.55am.

On the island, sirens sounded and residents reportedly heard fighter jets; Jeong Hae-seung, a 41-year-old working on a building site who spoke to the Hankyoreh newspaper, said he ran out of his workplace when the text arrived but could not make out what was being broadcast. Baek Un-bae told broadcaster YTN that an elderly resident had telephoned him asking whether war had broken out, noting older people with no media access were too alarmed to know how to respond. Others reported hearing nothing at all because their windows were shut against the cold and strong winds.

A second message from North Gyeongsang province — which administers Ulleungdo — said a flying object "presumed to be a North Korean aircraft" had left the danger zone, but the province acknowledged it had mistakenly used wording from its routine drill messages, changing only the time before sending it in error.

Jang described Tuesday's alert as unusual but could not confirm whether it was the first of its kind. The incident marked the fourth known entry by Russian military aircraft into the zone this year and the second within a week. An air defence identification zone is not sovereign airspace, though countries establish such zones beyond their own borders to identify incoming flights early; entering one without prior notification does not itself violate international law even when a flight plan has been submitted in advance.

Russia argues that the Korean zone lacks basis in international law and does not recognise Seoul's authority over it, having repeatedly flown into it without notice. According to data submitted to parliament, about 60 Russian entries without prior notification were recorded in the five years up to 2024, compared with about 430 by Chinese aircraft.

Seoul previously summoned Russia's defence attaché in March 2025 after eight entries occurred within 10 days — then described as the first such summons since a Russian aircraft violated South Korean airspace in 2019 and jets fired warning shots.
items.title: South Korea orders Ulleungdo residents to shelter after Russian military aircraft approach airspace

items.summary: Australia's new digital duty of care laws are set to pass parliament this week, with the Greens agreeing to support the bill after intense negotiations and extracting major amendments from Labor. Communications minister Anika Wells confirmed that social media and tech companies could face fines of up to 5% of their global revenue in extreme breaches, or a maximum of $109m if they flout the new laws. The legislation will apply online safety standards to social media, games, apps and chatbots, placing an overarching obligation on platforms 'to provide a safe online environment for all Australians' by replacing existing codes with a broader duty-of-care requirement to protect users from certain harmful content such as misogyny, terrorism, suicide, self-harm and eating disorders. Following discussions with the Greens, Wells confirmed amendments would give Australians a private right of action — a local equivalent allowing citizens to sue large companies in court. The government will consider setting up an independent ombudsman or watchdog for big tech, with the Telecommunications Industry Ombudsman volunteering to act as the complaints mechanism.
items.title: Australia's Digital Duty of Care Laws Pass After Greens Back Labor Bill

items.summary: An article translated from Chinese and authored by Zhang Haimei, a professor at Guangdong Institute of Public Administration (with views reflecting the author rather than CGTN), argues that China's anti-corruption campaign has evolved into significant "soft power" for attracting investment. The piece contends that amid high-quality development, corporate site-selection considerations have shifted away from short-term policy incentives toward stable and predictable business environments, clean political ecosystems, and properly regulated use of power. Citing the fourth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Commission for Discipline Inspection—which stressed targeting practices disrupting market order such as exploiting official positions for benefits, harsh attitudes, buck-passing, unauthorized fees, and profit-driven law enforcement—and the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee—calling to ensure officials "do not dare, are not able, and have no desire" to commit corruption—the author asserts that improving conduct, enforcing discipline, and fighting corruption has become a vital investment-attraction asset. The article identifies three dimensions through which anti-corruption supports this soft power: efficient government services, fair market competition, and cordial clean government-business relations. On standardized services, the piece claims integrated advancement of these principles brings key stages like project negotiation, market-access review, policy fulfillment, and factor support under institutional control to prevent opaque procedures; it attributes reforms such as "commencing construction immediately upon land acquisition" and "accessing benefits without application" to oversight mechanisms curbing buck-passing. On fair competition, the author argues anti-corruption efforts against government-business collusion reduce rent-seeking that skews resource allocation toward well-connected firms, enabling equal treatment in production-factor access, market-entry licensing, and operations. Regarding government-business relations, the article states these measures also address bureaucratic "lying-flat" inaction while opposing both overly close interactions where officials abuse power or enterprises capture officials for advantage, and overcautious distancing that leaves hidden administrative hurdles; it attributes local practices like regular government-business communication to curbing arbitrary power use and stabilizing policy environments. The author concludes that at the high-quality development stage, regional investment competition depends on business-environment stability and market fairness rather than incentive generosity, framing anti-corruption as institutional safeguards for lasting competitiveness.
items.title: Anti-Corruption Campaign as 'Soft Power' for Investment Attraction

items.summary: About 400,000 Malaysian citizens are currently barred from travelling over issues including unpaid taxes, court orders or outstanding payments to enforcement agencies, according to Malaysian Immigration Department director-general Zakaria Shaaban on Monday (Nov 23). Since 2024, a total of 404,848 Malaysians have been subjected to immigration travel restrictions, The Star reported. The Immigration Department acts on notifications from the Inland Revenue Board, the Department of Insolvency and other agencies but does not collect debts itself; Zakaria said anyone prevented from leaving due to outstanding liabilities must resolve the matter directly with the agency that imposed the restriction, and the department updates a person's status only when instructed by the relevant agency. Anyone found subject to an active arrest warrant or wanted-person notice would be referred to the relevant enforcement agency. Malaysians wanting to check their travel status before travelling are advised to visit the government's Immigration Travel Status Check website.
items.title: Malaysia Bars Over 400,000 Citizens from Travel for Unpaid Taxes and Outstanding Payments

items.summary: Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte said the alliance will defend every inch of its territory, including from threats in space, following intelligence reports that Russia was preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite. According to German media outlets NDR, WDR and Sueddeutsche Zeitung—citing anonymous military and intelligence sources—the Russian satellite, dubbed 'Sputnik-S,' would carry a nuclear warhead capable of disrupting or destroying other satellites, including communication and observation assets. The reports suggested a possible launch within 60 days; the authoring country was not identified. Rutte told a press conference in Berlin that Nato has various response options and regularly assesses its deterrence and defence posture. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he had not seen the latest reports but dismissed those citing 'unknown sources' as hardly worth taking seriously, while the Russian embassy in Berlin rejected what it called 'unfounded allegations,' describing them as part of a propaganda campaign. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz did not confirm or deny the reports but said they reveal the level of escalation Russia is evidently prepared to pursue, calling such plans no less shocking than previous ones. A German government spokesman also declined to confirm or deny the reports while saying it was taking them 'very seriously,' though warning against excessive nervousness regarding hypothetical dangers. European Space Agency head Josef Aschbacher called having nuclear weapons in space 'the ultimate nightmare scenario.' Russia is a signatory to the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, which bans weapons of mass destruction from orbit; other countries including the US and China have deployed or plan to deploy other types of space weaponry outside the treaty's scope. In 2024 the US claimed Russia was developing a nuclear-armed 'space-based' anti-satellite weapon that Moscow denied, with President Vladimir Putin reaffirming opposition to deploying nuclear weapons in space at the time.
items.title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after reports of Russian nuclear satellite

items.summary: Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, threatened Tuesday to close Switzerland's diplomatic office in retaliation for new sanctions imposed by the European country. The statement was carried by state news agency KCNA and denounced fresh Swiss sanctions targeting a camp in the North Korean city of Wonsan that hosts Chinese and Russian children. The Songdowon International Children's Camp has been accused of helping to indoctrinate Ukrainian children brought from Russian-occupied territories.
items.title: North Korea Threatens to Close Swiss Embassy Over Sanctions on Wonsan Children's Camp

items.summary: Japanese government bonds rallied across the curve after a three-day holiday, with gains holding even as domestic equities surged on easing concerns about artificial intelligence investment. The benchmark 10-year yield led the moves, falling 7 basis points to 2.715%, while five-year debt fell 5.5 basis points to 2.125%. The Nikkei stock average rose as much as 5% after Jensen Huang's return to lead Nvidia eased concerns about a slowdown in AI investment, showing JGBs holding firm even as risk appetite recovered.
items.title: Japanese Bonds Rally Across the Curve as Domestic Stocks Surge

items.summary: Finn Banks, a 16-year-old from the village of Congo near Batemans Bay on New South Wales's Far South Coast, won gold in the Men's Vision Impairment 2 division at the International Surfing Association's World Para Surfing Championships held in an artificial wave pool in Palm Desert, California. He scored 19.57 out of 20 overall — a perfect 10 on his opening final wave followed by a 9.57 — to become world champion overnight and the youngest member of Australia's Para Irukandjis surfing squad after joining it in August following two national titles at the Australian Para Surfing Championships in Byron Bay earlier this year, along with having claimed the 2026 Partial Vision Impairment Men's AASP World Tour Title at the 2026 Hawaii Adaptive Surfing Championships in May. Banks was born with low vision due to albinism and used the mechanical consistency of the wave pool to his advantage while being spotted by his father Russell, who said Banks handled the high-pressure environment well despite having only four waves in the final; he described feeling connected because he knew exactly what he wanted to do. Members of the Dalmeny Boardriders watched from Australia, with club president Matthew Hoar — who began coaching Banks three years ago through a surfing program run by St Peter's Anglican College in Broulee — saying the community was behind him and that Banks has inspired other young surfers joining the program. Australian surfer Kai Colless also won gold with a perfect score in the Men's Prone division, continuing his rivalry with Joel Taylor who took silver, while Emma Dieters from Sydney's Northern Beaches claimed bronze in the Kneel division alongside Byron Bay's Mark 'Mono' Stewart.
items.title: Australian teen Finn Banks wins gold at ISA World Para Surfing Championship

items.summary: Laura Stokes and her partner Adam Zerna, caretakers of the remote Berkeley River Lodge on Western Australia's Kimberley coast, are hoping for a less intense wet season after Tropical Cyclone Fina struck the property last November. The category three system made direct landfall in December 2025, destroying several accommodation villas, staff housing and solar infrastructure while Stokes and Zerna sheltered for 18 hours in an underground sea container before emerging to find sand dunes covered in debris with building materials scattered kilometres away. According to the Bureau of Meteorology, Fina holds a record as one of the earliest cyclones to impact mainland Australia alongside Cyclone Ines from November 1973; it had briefly reached category four strength and damaged homes in Darwin before hitting the lodge. Stokes said the owners debated whether they could reopen but ultimately decided to do so, with dozens of tradespeople flown to the air- and sea-accessible property to help rebuild against a tight window for opening day in May. The couple worked through the recovery over roughly 150 days while Stokes noted that vegetation had begun regenerating within weeks. Modelling by the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts predicts five to eight named cyclones between November 1 and April 30 this season, below average numbers; Stokes said she is hoping for a calmer wet season but described Berkeley as
items.title: Caretakers of Cyclone-Damaged WA Resort Hope for Quieter Wet Season

items.summary:
Australian music industry legend Molly Meldrum died aged 83 after a long illness, passing away peacefully at a hospital in Melbourne in the early hours of Monday morning. His family said he "passed away peacefully" and described him as affectionately dubbed 'the Guru', noting that "Molly was the heartbeat, the champion and the spirit of Australian music." Meldrum, born Ian Alexander Meldrum in Victoria in 1943, helped define Australia's music tastes for decades by championing local artists like INXS and Kylie Minogue alongside global acts such as Abba. He is known for his chaotic demeanour and trademark Stetson hat, having interviewed a wide array of stars throughout his career.

Meldrum hosted the Australian Broadcasting Corporation's music television programme Countdown and later appeared on a segment of variety show Hey Hey, It's Saturday. In 2014 he became the first person who was not a recording artist to be inducted into the Australian Recording Industry Association (Aria) Hall of Fame. He lived with an acquired brain injury after falling from a ladder in 2011.

King Charles paid tribute on Monday, calling Meldrum "a true giant of the music industry." The king reflected on his most famous interview with Meldrum—a 1977 sit-down for Countdown's 40th anniversary special—in which Meldrum could not calm his jitters and stumbled over his lines, declaring: "Your Royal Highness... Oh, oh, I'm sweating like a pig." King Charles said of the infamous interview: "There is an old showbusiness saying which warns never to work with animals or children. But nobody prepared me for Molly Meldrum." An aide to the King said he had been "deeply saddened" to hear of Meldrum's death and hoped that his interview would once again raise a few smiles as Australians honour Meldrum's legacy.

Elton John, described as a friend and regular interviewee, paid tribute to Meldrum as "an Australian legend and an institution." Pop star Kylie Minogue said she would be turning up the music in his honour, recalling watching him on Countdown every weekend as a child. Australia's Arts Minister Tony Burke said the country had lost an icon, noting that one of Meldrum's greatest legacies will be the generations of Australians who grew up with his unmistakable enthusiasm and love of music.
items.title: King Charles, Elton John Pay Tribute to Deceased Australian Music Legend Molly Meldrum

items.summary: At its annual session in Berlin, NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte warned of "intensifying malign activities targeting our nations," coming amid a fresh wave of security incidents across Europe including hybrid attacks and airspace violations. The NATO Parliamentary Assembly held the meeting as these concerns grew alongside ongoing questions about prospects for peace in Ukraine.
items.title: NATO Secretary General Warns of Intensifying Threats Amid European Security Incidents

items.summary: A fire at Makofi Hotel near the northern tip of Nungwi Beach in Tanzania swept into adjacent resorts, restaurants, and shops after strong winds carried flames along thatched roofs. Eyewitness footage showed buildings roaring with flames as tourists and locals evacuated before firefighters from three stations subdued the blaze after roughly three hours. Although several hotel staff were injured, officials confirmed all 183 tourists escaped unharmed; more than 20 hotels in Mchangani and Matemwe offered free accommodation to displaced guests across six affected properties (Makofi, Z Hotel, Nungwi Garden, BR, Pasha, and Sand Beach), four restaurants, and about 40 shops. Investigators were still determining whether the fire originated in a bread-baking oven as early accounts suggested, while Tourism and Antiquities Minister Nasra Nassor Omar urged patience ahead of an official inquiry and promised a rapid assessment to guide the government's response.
items.title: Fire Engulfs Beachfront Hotels on Zanzibar's Nungwi Beach

items.summary: At the FIFA Under-17 World Cup, Senegal defeated Cuba 9-0 in a match that moved them to the top of Group F with four points. The result left them level on points with Croatia, whom they had drawn against in their opening match. A player said the team had prepared carefully and executed its plans during training without any surprise element. “Technically, it was good, but it was something we did during training and we repeated it. There was no surprise,” he stated. The coach praised the squad’s preparation and clinical finishing, saying they have a well-studied team that spends hours analyzing opponents’ strengths and weaknesses before matches. He added that on this occasion “the players understood the areas to use and were effective in front of goal.” Senegal now face Tajikistan in their final group match, with qualification for the round of 32 at stake.
items.title: Senegal U17s Rout Cuba 9-0 to Top Group F at FIFA Under-17 World Cup

items.summary: Going into this year's U.N. climate talks held in Turkey, expectations were already low, but the outcome was worse than anticipated: negotiators failed to reach an overall agreement amid frequent extreme weather events linked to climate change. The collapse centered on a single point of contention—whether to include language about fossil fuels, described as the main driver of global warming. This dispute had been building for years; during previous conferences, nations repeatedly threatened to walk away unless they secured strong agreements on fossil fuels, and in those instances negotiators ultimately voiced their disagreements in closing plenaries before falling into line. This time, however, many countries were unwilling to do so.
items.title: U.N. Climate Talks Collapse Over Fossil Fuel Language

items.summary: Hailey Bieber, who turned 30 on November 22, has established herself as a self-made star and the founder of Rhode, the cosmetics brand she built into a billion-dollar business in three years. Born to actor Stephen Baldwin and raised amid Hollywood connections, she pursued ballet before an injury ended that path at a young age, then began modeling at 18. She stepped away from runway work after a bad experience with a casting director who undermined her confidence, telling Allure in 2022 that she did not want to feel small in a space where she felt good about other work. Global fame came through her relationship with singer Justin Bieber, which began when Stephen Baldwin brought Hailey to the Today show at age 15 while Bieber performed there in 2009; they met as teenagers and spent time together before rumors of romance emerged after Bieber split from Selena Gomez at the end of 2014. The pair's relationship evolved through a
items.title: Hailey Bieber Turns 30 as Founder of Billion-Dollar Beauty Empire Rhode

items.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi received a low-key welcome at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, where mobile stairs fell about 40 centimeters short of her aircraft door threshold and no musical performances or cheering crowds were provided. Japan's Yomiuri newspaper reported on November 20 that when she met Chinese leader Xi Jinping at the dinner reception his reaction was cold, and unlike other regional leaders who managed brief one-on-one meetings with Xi, the Japanese delegation was not granted such access. William Yang, a Taiwan-based analyst for the International Crisis Group, told DW that the frostiness from China's side was on full display from the moment Takaichi's plane landed, said he could think of no reason other than deliberate intent behind the steps issue, and noted the ice did not break when she tried to speak with Xi at the dinner reception. The summit snub comes amid a sharp downturn in bilateral relations that began in November 2025 when Takaichi told Japan's Diet any contingency involving Taiwan would also threaten Japanese national security; David Adebahr, a professor of international relations and Asia-Pacific security policy at Kobe University, said to DW she was merely stating what had long been the internal logic of Japanese security planning. Beijing has demanded that Takaichi retract her statement while restricting rare earth mineral exports critical to Japan's industry, banning imports of Japanese seafood, and advising tourists to remove Japan from their destination lists. Adebahr told DW that Beijing believes it holds more cards than in the past due to Japan's dependence on Chinese rare earths, an increasingly visible military presence around Japan sometimes in conjunction with Russia, and a US administration urging Tokyo to de-escalate rather than firmly backing it, which he said left China with little incentive to offer Takaichi a face-saving compromise. Yang told DW that as a committed conservative who has talked tough on Beijing's rapid military buildup, island seizures in the South China Sea, and pressure on Taiwan, Takaichi cannot give in to Xi's demands for fear of losing face with her hardline base, describing this as a major test of her abilities and wisdom. Yang forecasted that China would maintain its current approach by continuing to step up pressure through limiting targeted exports and amplifying assertions with Russia and North Korea that Japan is embracing remilitarization, while Japan was likely to seek opportunities to signal goodwill in return for small-scale compromises; he added a reset depended on how the Trump administration shaped foreign policy for the remainder of his presidency. Adebahr told DW that although diplomatic relations would remain frosty, complex interdependence over trade, technology and critical minerals—now seen as security issues—would prevent full decoupling because transaction costs would be far too high for both sides.
items.title: Japan's APEC Snub Highlights Frosty China Ties Under New PM

items.summary: On Monday, Finland said it had summoned Russia's ambassador over a suspected violation of Finnish airspace by a Russian helicopter. The summons came in the wake of two recent events: a Ukrainian drone strike that hit a Russian cargo ship identified as the Sparta II in international waters in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday, and hours later a suspected Russian helicopter intrusion into Nordic airspace. According to Finnish authorities—with help from Estonian and Russian rescue vessels—the fire aboard the vessel was extinguished after it had drifted into Finnish waters and anchored about 90 kilometres east of Helsinki; the ship's crew were evacuated with one person suffering minor wounds before the vessel was towed back to Russia on Sunday evening. In its statement, Finland's foreign ministry condemned Moscow's strikes against civilian targets in Ukraine as part of what it called an illegal war of aggression, described Russia's actions in Europe as dangerous and reckless, and affirmed solidarity with Denmark, Poland, and other European partners while noting that Ukraine has the right to defend itself.
items.title: Finland Summons Russian Ambassador After Suspected Airspace Violation and Drone Strike on Cargo Ship

items.summary: The State Bank of India (SBI) has advised the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to consider a modest 25 basis points rate hike in its December monetary policy rather than a jumbo 50 bps increase, warning that an aggressive move could trigger capital outflows, currency instability, and concerns over economic growth. The report emphasized the need for financial stability amid growing global market uncertainty as it prepared ahead of the RBI Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting scheduled for December 2–4, with the policy decision to be announced on December 4.
items.title: SBI Advises RBI on Cautious 25 bps Hike Amid Calls for Jumbo Rate Cut

items.summary:
South Indian Bank (SIB) disclosed that the Reserve Bank of India has approved SBI Mutual Fund's acquisition of up to 9.99 per cent of the bank's paid-up share capital or voting rights, as reported in a regulatory filing published on November 24, 2026. The approval is conditional on compliance with the Banking Regulation Act, 1949; RBI directions governing commercial banks' acquisition and holding of shares or voting rights; the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999; Securities and Exchange Board of India regulations; and any other applicable statutes, regulations, and guidelines.

As at September-end 2026, public shareholding in South Indian Bank stood at 100 per cent. Mutual funds collectively held a 15.13 per cent stake in the Thrissur (Kerala)-headquartered private sector bank, distributed across Kotak Mahindra Trustee Co Ltd's A/C Kotak Multicap Fund (6.05 per cent), Bandhan Small Cap Fund (4.69 per cent), and SBI Banking & Financial Services Fund (2.90 per cent).
items.title: RBI Approves SBI Mutual Fund to Acquire Up to 9.99% of South Indian Bank

items.summary: Following NVIDIA's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO, Krishnamoorthi posted on X urging House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast to hold a full public hearing with Huang. He argued that Congress and the American public deserve transparency about what Chinese intelligence may have obtained from Huang and whether advanced American AI technology was compromised, insisting such questions be answered publicly rather than behind closed doors. His demand comes amid growing scrutiny of NVIDIA over allegations concerning possible Chinese intelligence links and the diversion of advanced American semiconductor products for military applications in China. Krishnamoorthi stated that Trump Administration's rush to reinstate Huang underscores the need for Congress to act, accusing it of putting its own financial interests before national security, and pledged Democratic investigations into any wrongdoing by the administration, Huang, other NVIDIA executives, and anyone selling out national security for financial gain, while also pursuing bipartisan policies to stop advanced technology flowing to China. Meanwhile, Vice President JD Vance welcomed Huang's return on X with a post reading 'Welcome back Jensen.' According to a Financial Times report, disclosures of Trump's investment portfolio through the end of September indicated his NVIDIA holdings had potentially increased in value by approximately USD 15 million. Trump subsequently acknowledged speaking to NVIDIA's board regarding Huang's position and told CNBC he did not use the word 'prosecuted' but assured the company that 'he's absolutely fine,' adding that if he thought Huang did something wrong, he would not recommend his reinstatement. US lawmakers maintained that NVIDIA's internal investigation and the board's decision do not resolve broader national security concerns; House Select Committee on China Chairman John Moolenaar (R-MI), House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence Chairman Rick Crawford (R-AR), and House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast (R-FL) issued a joint statement saying the company's internal review does not erase the threats that must be addressed, noting Huang and Tim Teter confirmed they will appear for transcribed interviews on December 1 and December 2 as planned. NVIDIA announced Monday that Huang had been reinstated with immediate effect as President and CEO and Board member; according to a statement from NVIDIA's Board of Directors, the unanimous decision followed discussions and meetings with Huang, who apologized to employees upon returning to headquarters in Santa Clara, California, saying 'I've made some very terrible mistakes.'
items.title: Krishnamoorthi Urges Public Hearing With Nvidia's Jensen Huang Amid National Security Scrutiny

items.summary: President Trump publicly praised the reinstatement of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, telling The New York Times that Huang had 'worked it out' with his wife Lori Huang. Speaking in an interview published Monday after Nvidia's board voted to reinstate Huang as chief executive, Trump said, 'He's got a very, very, very good wife, and they've worked it out,' adding that 'She's a fantastic woman.' He was referring to Lori Huang, a major Nvidia shareholder who has not spoken publicly since reports emerged about her husband's close relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman unrelated to him. Trump also backed the board's decision in writing, stating on social media that 'The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO,' and arguing that 'The Country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy.' He said he had no reason to believe Huang's return posed a national security risk, noting that the attorney general confirmed the government did not have evidence of unlawful conduct by Huang. Trump described himself as having 'gotten to know Jensen,' calling him 'a Great Patriot and National Treasure,' while also urging Nvidia to continue its internal investigation into whether the company complied with U.S. export controls so it could fulfill what he called its 'Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security.' He had earlier urged the board on Truth Social that bringing Huang back would be 'the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A.,' telling CNBC that he 'convinced them' and 'made the deal.' Separately, reports estimated a possible divorce settlement exceeding $60 billion — with one estimate reaching $81.1 billion based on Huang's reported net worth at the time under California community property laws assuming an equal division of marital assets; however, neither Jensen nor Lori Huang had announced a divorce, and these figures were hypothetical estimates rather than confirmed payments. The couple have been married since 1985 and have two children.
items.title: Trump Praises Jensen Huang's Return to Nvidia and Comments on His Marriage

items.summary: A joint investigation by German newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung and public broadcasters NDR and WDR reports that Western intelligence agencies, including the Bundeswehr and Germany's Federal Intelligence Service (BND), assess Moscow intends to launch a satellite equipped with nuclear explosives as early as this year. The findings were shared among several NATO countries in recent days, and Bundeswehr experts reportedly briefed senior German politicians, including Defence Minister Boris Pistorius of the SPD. A spokesperson for Germany's Federal Ministry of Defence cited secrecy and confidentiality while stating that officials are continuously monitoring developments in space and other states' activities. Russian state news agency TASS reported that Security Council Deputy Chairman Dmitry Medvedev asserted that actions by Ukraine and NATO have created circumstances under which Moscow weighs potential use of nuclear weapons, though he emphasized restraint and proportionality before any strike. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called the reports shocking but not new, while NATO Chief Mark Rutte said the alliance is assessing its deterrence and defence capabilities across land, sea, air and space. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reiterated that NATO membership remains Ukraine's clearest security guarantee. During historic trilateral talks with US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, Putin echoed shared global stewardship while Trump said the three largest nuclear powers are positioned to discuss reducing arsenals; following the summit, the countries adopted a joint Declaration towards Peace reaffirming that a nuclear war cannot be won or fought.
items.title: German Intelligence Warns Russia May Place Nuclear Weapon in Space by Year-End

Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as its chief executive officer, reversing a decision made just 11 days earlier after revelations about his reported extramarital relationships. The announcement triggered a sharp rally in the company's shares, adding $952 billion to its market value in a single trading session and pushing Nvidia shares up more than 30%, which CNN described as their third-best trading day on record; the Nasdaq Composite rose 6.51%. Forbes estimated Huang's fortune at approximately $143 billion, reflecting a single-day increase of $33 billion.

The reinstatement followed an intervention by US President Donald Trump, who mobilized senior administration officials to persuade Nvidia's board to bring Huang back. According to people familiar with the matter cited by CNN, Trump had been concerned about the impact of Huang's departure on the stock market and broader US economy, concluding that restoring the CEO was necessary to stabilize investor confidence and prevent the country from losing a key figure in the global AI race. Trump personally contacted board members to vouch for Huang, whom he considers critical to America's artificial intelligence ambitions and its economic competition with China.

Vice President JD Vance led the White House pressure campaign, becoming the administration's principal emissary using his connections in Silicon Valley. The Associated Press reported that Vance stepped up his involvement over the weekend to make Trump's case to the board, and CNN reported that he coordinated directly with Huang over 72 hours, assuring the board that the government had found no evidence that the CEO committed anything illegal or threatened national security. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent were also involved in the effort according to CNN.

According to news agency Reuters, US Attorney General Todd Blanche and Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton played roles in determining Huang was not a security risk to the US and saw no evidence he did anything illegal or untoward related to national security. Speaking to CNBC on Monday, Trump acknowledged his role in the decision, saying "I believe my intervention was very important," adding that he had spoken to Huang on Sunday and that the executive promised to work harder following his return.

The intervention followed concerns about Huang's reported extramarital relationships, including one involving Alice Huang, a woman US officials suspected could have links to Chinese intelligence. Another relationship reportedly involved a direct subordinate. Nvidia's board said it would complete its investigation into the national security concerns. Meanwhile, the Commerce Department is adding Megaspeed — where Alice Huang was an executive and which purchased Nvidia chips that US officials feared could reach China — to the US Entity List, restricting its access to US exports according to a notice scheduled for publication in the Federal Register.

Huang is scheduled to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next Thursday, where questions about his conduct, Nvidia's China strategy and the administration's intervention are expected to remain under scrutiny.
items.title: Trump and Vance pressure campaign leads White House to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO
