A report released by SBI Research on Tuesday urged the Reserve Bank of India to prioritise financial stability in its upcoming December monetary policy meeting, recommending that a 25 basis points (bps) repo rate hike would be sufficient to address the prevailing inflation trajectory rather than an aggressive 50 bps increase. The research warned that a jumbo rate hike could trigger unintended economic consequences—including capital outflows, rupee volatility, and slower economic growth—particularly amid mounting global financial uncertainty and growing pressure on international equity markets.

The report also examined vulnerabilities in the US housing sector during November, noting that US mortgage debt has reached $13.3 trillion while consumer credit interest rates remain elevated at 11.9%, which SBI Research said is increasing household debt servicing costs and weakening housing affordability and demand. The research observed that despite homeowner equity standing at around 110% of US GDP, housing mobility remains constrained as existing borrowers are reluctant to surrender their previously secured lower mortgage rates.

Addressing investor behaviour amid growing economic uncertainty, the report highlighted a shift toward gold exchange-traded funds (ETFs), which recorded net inflows of $706 million during the first fortnight of November—reversing net outflows of $657 million in October. SBI Research drew parallels with previous financial crises, when it noted that precious metal prices recovered sharply while equity markets remained under pressure.

On exchange rate management, the report emphasised the importance of currency stability amid changing global financial conditions, arguing that movements beyond a certain threshold could amplify economic shocks rather than absorb them. Against this backdrop, SBI Research concluded that a measured interest rate increase would help the RBI balance inflation management, financial stability, and economic growth without intensifying existing market vulnerabilities.
items.title: SBI Research Advocates a Calibrated 25 Bps Rate Hike Ahead of the RBI's December Policy Meeting

items.summary:
President Donald Trump claimed credit for persuading Nvidia’s board to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang, telling CNBC that his administration had given the directors assurances about national security implications of the return. Speaking on the network, Trump said he was represented at a board meeting and later stated he spoke directly with the directors and convinced them to bring Huang back; when asked whether he assured them Huang would not face prosecution, he replied that he did not use the word prosecuted but provided sufficient reassurance. He defended his intervention as serving the national interest while declining to announce an investment plan or a fixed formula for intervening in corporate leadership.

Three Republican congressional committee chairmen said the reinstatement does not end their scrutiny of Nvidia’s dealings with China, issuing a joint statement that the board’s brief internal investigation and Huang’s return do not erase the national security threats and questions that must be addressed. The lawmakers identified concerns about suspected large-scale smuggling of Nvidia products, diversion for Chinese military purposes, and contributions to China’s artificial intelligence capabilities, noting these remain subjects of inquiry rather than established findings.

The three chairmen are Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, John Moolenaar of the Select Committee on China, and Rick Crawford of the House Intelligence Committee. They said Huang and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter had confirmed they would attend interviews previously scheduled for December 1 and December 2; those arrangements were announced November 17 as transcribed interviews with formally recorded answers.

Nvidia separately reported its board voted unanimously to restore Huang as president, chief executive, and a director effective immediately, stating that discussions satisfied directors about his candor and ability to lead. The company said input from senior US government officials gave the board confidence that his reinstatement posed no national security risk while an independent directors’ investigation continues; Nvidia launched that inquiry following reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort.

Nvidia also stated it would continue cooperating with government investigations, that Huang supported and will cooperate with the ongoing inquiry, and that its board has established a committee overseeing national security and export-control risks. The company is searching for a chief compliance officer.
items.title: Trump Credits Role in Jensen Huang’s Nvidia Return; Lawmakers Continue China Chip Probe

items.summary:
Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang returned to the company's headquarters in Santa Clara, California, on Monday after its board unanimously reinstated him as president and chief executive officer. Employees greeted his return with a loud ovation following a video message he shared, in which he thanked them for giving him “a second chance” and said he intended to be a better CEO. Huang had stepped down earlier that month amid reports of alleged extramarital affairs, including two involving Nvidia employees and another with a woman allegedly tied to China; the allegations remain under scrutiny while Nvidia conducts an independent investigation into his reported relationship with Alice Huang. In announcing the reinstatement, Nvidia's board said it was satisfied with Huang's “candor” on the matter and that his return “poses no national security risk,” citing input from senior US government officials. Board chair Harvey Jones stated the company believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia and expressed confidence in working with him as he resumes leadership.

President Donald Trump claimed credit for Huang's reinstatement, telling CNBC on Monday that he had spoken with the board and “convinced them” to bring the co-founder back. Huang has been a Trump ally who previously lobbied his administration to allow Nvidia to sell its advanced H200 chips to China.

Huang's return coincided with a sharp rally in Nvidia shares and the broader US stock market. According to figures reported, Nvidia stock jumped 31.48% on Monday — its biggest one-day gain since 2003 and its third-best session on record — adding $952 billion to the company's market value in a single day. The stock climbed as much as 36.6% before paring gains, helping fuel a wider technology-led rally with the Nasdaq Composite rising 6.51% and the S&P 500 gaining 4.73%; both indexes recorded their biggest single-session gains since April 2025.

Huang's return does not end scrutiny of the company. Senate Banking Committee chairman Tim Scott said Huang would testify before the panel on December 3, amid continuing questions around national security and Nvidia's dealings involving China.
items.title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO Amid Stock Surge

items.summary: Transcripts of recorded phone calls released by the US government show Indian national Nikhil Gupta discussing multiple assassination targets, including one in Canada. The 55-year-old was recently sentenced to nearly 20 years in prison for his role in Gurpatwant Singh Pannun's murder-for-hire case. In a June 19, 2023 conversation with an undercover officer he believed was a hitman named "Carlos," Gupta spoke just one day after the killing of pro-Khalistan separatist Hardeep Singh Nijjar outside a gurudwara in Canada. He forwarded what prosecutors said was a video clip of Nijjar's body, stating they had several targets and that they now had approval to proceed without waiting. In a separate conversation on June 20, Gupta warned the confidential informant "Pacho" that Pannun would become more cautious following Nijjar's death and instructed them to change individuals monitoring Pannun regularly while cautioning about possible FBI attention. Earlier transcripts show Gupta confirming he wanted to kill Pannun for $25,000, which he described as "very small money," with the payment reportedly reaching New York by June 6.

items.summary:
According to a tradition handed down through generations, the Cochin royal family traces its origin to a Namboothiri of Perumpadappu Mana who married a sister of the last Perumal; lacking heirs from his brahmin wife, he bequeathed his wealth and landed estates to his kshatriya wife and their son, who adopted the Perumpadappu name. When the Perumal kingdom was partitioned, the monarch granted the central portion—including the royal capital at Mahodayapuram—to this sister's son, who became Valiya Thampuran (Raja of Perumpadappu Swaroopam) as his legal heir under matriliny. The territory reportedly ran from Pookaitha in the north to Kannetti in the south, with overlordship of the Thiruvanchikulam Temple at Mahodayapuram passing along with it; this geographic reach is considered plausible since Vanneri (where Perumpadappu lies today) sits within Ponnani taluk and Kollam formed the northern limit of Venad rule. C Achyuta Menon, in The Cochin State Manual, places the northernmost limit at Vanneri but restricts the southern boundary to Purakkad (present-day Alappuzha district), estimating the whole country—including its tributary states—at roughly 4,000 square miles.

The coronation rite known as Ariyittuvazhcha was held at Chitrakutam in Vanneri before the family lost access to it after being driven out by enemies. The Paliyam copper plates of 1663 mention both Perumpadappu and Chitrakutam, with the Raja complaining that troubles stemmed from negligence at Chitrakutum in not worshipping deities properly and urging his nephews (anantaravars) to recover "Perumpadappu and other lost territories." The dynasty's extent is attributed to matriliny: children born to a woman belong to her kin-group, so the son of the Perumpadappu Namboothiri and the Perumal's sister belonged to his mother's kshatriya lineage rather than being regarded as a Namboothiri. For this reason, scholars generally hold that members of Perumpadappu Swaroopam are lineal descendants of the Perumals and that kingship passed to the Perumpadappu Raja—a tradition observed by the Cochin royal family well into the closing decades of the 20th century.

A matrilineal family unit consisted of a woman, her children, and her grandchildren; as branches proliferated, each daughter's household developed into a separate thavazhi. The Perumpadappu Raja is said to have had five sisters—Mootha (elder), Elaya (younger), Palluruthy, Muringur (Madattumkeezhil), and Chazhur—the last three named for their settlement places; each thavazhi received a kovilakam, titles, privileges, land revenue, its own armed retinue, and rights over certain temples. Succession followed the maternal line, with adoption from another thavazhi when heirs were lacking; across thavazhis, the most senior male became Valiya Thampuran (Senior Raja) while the next in line became Elaya Thampuran (Junior Raja), and similarly the most senior female was Valiyamma Thampuran (Senior Rani) followed by Kunjamma Thampuran (Junior Rani). A tradition developed whereby a Raja could abdicate due to old age or poor health, going into religious seclusion; upon his death, a regent from the same thavazhi made way for the heir apparent and also went into seclusion.

The Rajas bore the title "Perumpadappu Gangadhara Trikkovil Adhikarikal." "Gangadhara" alludes to Lord Shiva of the Thiruvanchikulam Mahadeva Temple at Mahodayapuram—the Perumals' patron deity, which passed under the Raja's supervision along with the capital and remains important to the family today. "Trikkovil Adhikarikal" denotes royal-officer status; as Professor MGS Narayanan notes, "Koyil Adhikarikal" can be read as "a prince of the Cera dynasty." The family also holds that its kuladevatha, Pazhayannur Bhagavathy, was originally the tutelary deity of the Perumpadappu Namboothiri and later adopted by the Swaroopam; shrines to her stand at Pazhayannur in old Thalappilly taluk (present-day Thrissur district), Mattancherry Palace in Cochin, Chazhur's kovilakam, and Puthen Bungalow Temple at Tripunithura. The Bhagavathy witnessed the 1663 copper plate treaty with the Dutch.

The family also adopted local deities of their residences as paradevathas: Koippilly Narayanan Temple (dedicated to Lord Shiva and Vishnu, deity Koippilly Thevar) at Perumpadappu in Vanneri near Naranippuzha; Thiruvanchikulam Appan (Lord Shiva) at Kodungallur; and Sree Poornathrayeesa at Tripunithura. Members of the royal household still fund ritual offerings to Koippilly Thevar.

The earliest mention of Perumpadappu Swaroopam appears in the Elankunnapuzha Kshethra Grandhavari, concerning construction of the Elankunnapuzha Temple on Vypeen Island (formed after the 1341 great Periyar flood and situated north of Cochin). The chronogram reads "Visvesa Sakti Maya," corresponding to 1185–1186 CE. A free transliteration records that after an idol's installation by Uliyannur Mekatt Namboothiri around 1185–86 CE, a temple official of Vypeen Elankunnapuzha Temple went to Cochin to inform the Valiya Thampuran; the entry concludes that land from the mouth of the Vypeen River (Vaypa Azhikkal) northwards to Munambam belonged to Perumpadappu Swaroopam. The earliest extant personal reference is the Syrian Christian copper plate grant of Vira Raghava, dated 1225 CE, which records privileges for merchant Iravikorttan and was issued by "the glorious Vira-Raghava-Chakravartin" ruling from his palace at Magodaiyarpattinam (Mahodayapuram); since Mahodayapuram passed to the Swaroopam, historians identify him as a Perumpadappu Raja, with ancestor "Vira-Kerala-Chakravartin" possibly being the first ruler.

Scholars have pieced together a tentative chronology from inscriptions, mortgage deeds, grandhavaris, and literature. VKR Menon (Maharaja's College, Ernakulam) lists Rama Varma as Raja in 1330 CE, probably still ruling in 1337 when he received privileges at the Irinjalakuda Temple; a 1352 grant to an east-coast brahmin is recorded. Documents from 1451 and 1452 mention "Perumpadappil Mootha kovilakam" (Mootha thavazhi) without personal names, while an Urakam inscription of 1452 CE refers to Narayana Ravi Varma of the Elaya thavazhi. Mortgage deeds dated 1455 and 1463 mention Sree Vira Govinda Kota Varma; a Swarnathumana Grantham entry records "Rama Varma Rayira Tirukoyiladhikarikal," and an undated (or separately noted) entry mentions Unni Rama Varma of the Elaya thavazhi. Portuguese accounts indicate that in December 1500, terms were struck at Cochin with a Raja called Unni Rama Koil.

Taken together, these historical, geographical, epigraphical, literary, oral, and familial data support the tradition that Perumpadappu in Vanneri is the Swaroopam's place of origin, suggest it already existed in the 12th century, and indicate—in accordance with matrilineal succession—that the Perumal's nephew became the Perumpadappu Raja. This text is excerpted from The Making of Cochin: A Royal Family's Chronicles of War and Survival by Kocha Rama Varma, Usha Chettur Varma, and Rajith B Nair (Westland).
items.title: Origin and Early History of the Perumpadappu Swaroopam Royal Dynasty

items.summary: Exiled Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina announced plans to return to Bangladesh on December 16 — Victory Day, which commemorates the surrender of Pakistani forces in 1971 and marks independence. The date was revealed through a statement by her spokesperson Syed Mozammel Ali on Tuesday (November 24), marking the first time she has specified a return date after more than two years in exile. Hasina, who fled Bangladesh aboard a Bangladesh Air Force aircraft on August 5, 2024 following student-led protests that ended her 15-year tenure as prime minister, now calls on Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's government to arrange her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka via Biman Bangladesh Airlines. Ali stated: 'Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka.' Her proposed return comes amid a polarized political environment, mounting legal challenges, and strained relations between Dhaka and New Delhi. Hasina, aged 79, has remained in India since arriving on August 5, 2024.
items.title: Ousted Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina Sets December 16 Return Date, Urges Tarique Government to Arrange Flight from India

In a series of posts on X, Das said he had been invited by the Oxford University Students' Union for a panel discussion and delivered talks on the 'cockroach movement,' but discovered upon reaching the check that his passport had been flagged. He accused the Modi government of preventing him from traveling to attend events at prestigious institutions including Cambridge, LSE, and Edinburgh, claiming the incident would not deter him from future travel to London, Paris, and other locations. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacted on X by alleging that 'someone in power' was jealous of Das receiving an invitation from Oxford.
items.title: CJP's Saurav Das Alleges Delhi Airport Denial of Flight to London for Oxford Lecture

The quake occurred at a depth of 20 km (6.2 miles) with its epicentre located at latitude 27.855 N and longitude 87.909 E, per reports from EMSC and the National Center for Seismology. The USGS separately reported that the magnitude 5.3 earthquake was recorded about 67 km WNW of Mangan, India.
items.title: Magnitude 5.3 Earthquake Strikes Nepal's Koshi Province, Tremors Felt Across Parts of India

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi marked the Parkash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji on Monday, speaking at a Shabad Kirtan programme in New Delhi. He highlighted the Sikh Gurus' teachings of devotion, equality, service and universal welfare, describing Gurbani and kirtan as forms of spiritual practice rather than mere music. Modi recalled Guru Nanak's principles of 'Kirat Karo, Vand Chhako, Naam Japo,' which he said remained central to his life, while also referencing the Sikh prayer 'Nanak Naam Chardi Kala, Tere Bhane Sarbat Da Bhala' and its message of seeking welfare for everyone. This year's observance coincided with the 350th anniversary of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji's martyrdom in Delhi; Modi recalled his sacrifice for faith and belief while paying tribute to Bhai Mati Das Ji, Bhai Sati Das Ji, Bhai Dayala Ji, Sardar Teja Singh Samundri, Mata Gujri Ji and the Sahibzadas. He said the Sikh Gurus played an important role in preserving India's cultural identity during difficult periods and that their teachings would continue to guide the country toward Viksit Bharat. Modi listed several initiatives over the past 12 years commemorating the Gurus, including celebrations of the 350th Parkash Purab of Guru Gobind Singh Ji, the 550th Parkash Purab of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, and national events at Red Fort marking the 400th Parkash Purab of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji. He also referred to Veer Bal Diwas on December 26 as an occasion to introduce younger generations to the courage and sacrifice of these figures, noted his recent visit to the Khalsa Diwan Gurdwara in the Philippines where he said the government is supporting redevelopment efforts, and called for collective action by families, gurdwaras, religious congregations and social organisations to protect young people from drug abuse. Modi described substance abuse among youth as a serious social challenge and expressed confidence that collective efforts inspired by the Sikh Gurus' teachings would help build a better future.
items.title: PM Modi Pays Tribute to Guru Nanak Dev Ji on Parkash Purab
